subject: Onboarding Benchmarking — Canary Gates, KV-cache Scenarios, and Evidence Package
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@payglide.com>

Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@payglide.com>
Date: 2028-11-01T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sandbox access + initial benchmarking questions

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today — excited to get PayGlide onto Redwood for production inference. Before we lock in dates for a formal benchmark sprint, Samir and I sketched the most important questions from our side:

- We need to validate cold-start behavior for occasional batch jobs (predominantly CPU->GPU start).
- Expected throughput for our 8k-conversation-per-day workload: would like a recommended peak target and an average baseline.
- Clarity on what artifacts you’ll deliver as the canonical evidence for acceptance (logs, latency histograms, kv-cache heatmaps, token-cost summary).

Can you propose a brief runbook we can sign off on? We want to involve security and SRE early so they can assess artifact retention and redaction requirements.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Product
PayGlide

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@payglide.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@payglide.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-02T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding Benchmarking — Canary Gates, KV-cache Scenarios, and Evidence Package

Hi Alicia / Samir — great to hear. I’ve attached a one-page sprint plan and an initial list of canary gates. TL;DR: we recommend a two-phase benchmark run over 72 hours with staged validation:

Phase A (synthetic correctness + steady-state throughput) — 24h
- Target steady throughput: 1,200 req/s aggregate across the tenant (peak bursts up to 1,800).
- Latency targets: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 300ms, p99 < 700ms for the hosted model variant; cold-start p95 < 2.5s.
- Error rate gate: overall request error rate < 0.5%; per-minute spikes allowed up to 1% for < 5 minutes.

Phase B (KV-cache warm/cold + model-variant fallbacks) — 48h
- Scenarios: cold-cache (no prefix hits), warm-cache (80% prefix KV hits), mixed (gradual traffic shift).
- Canary pass criteria: no regression beyond 10% in p95 vs Phase A after model variant switch.

Deliverables from Redwood: artifact bundle (latency histograms, raw request traces, KV hit-rate logs, token-cost breakdown), runbook steps, and a short pass/fail decision note. I’ve proposed owners inline in the attached spreadsheet.

Security / retention note: we will redact any customer payloads in logged traces; full request IDs, timestamps, and anonymized trace IDs will be shipped. Monica will follow up with our compliance checklist for artifact retention.

Next steps: if that looks good, can Samir confirm the target weekend window (Nov 7–9) and any blackout periods? Once we get your go-ahead I’ll book the Dedicated pool and provision the canary config.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: payglide_benchmark-plan-v1.xlsx, canary-gate-definitions.md

Subject: Re: Onboarding Benchmarking — Canary Gates, KV-cache Scenarios, and Evidence Package

Hi Samir — quick answers inline.

On Nov 3, 2028, Samir Patel wrote:
> 1) For the cold-cache runs we want an explicit measurement of cold start tail latency for the first 100 requests after a model-container recycle — can you make that a named artifact?

Yes — we will extract a "cold-start-first-100" histogram and include per-container boot times. That will show both the kernel init and the first-token latencies.

> 2) We’ll need a short SLA note that we can include in our internal change advisory: if the canary fails, what rollback steps will Redwood execute automatically vs what requires manual action?

Automatic behavior: if canary violation > configured threshold (we recommend 3 consecutive 5-min windows where p95 exceeds gate by >25% or error rate >1%), the router will divert 100% traffic to the previously pinned model variant and mark the new variant as quarantined. Manual: capacity-level interventions (resizing Dedicated pool) require ops approval. I'll paste a short version for your advisory:

- If canary fails: immediate automated rollback to pinned variant; notifications to PayGlide SRE and Redwood ops; isolated artifact collection for postmortem.
- If capacity breach: Redwood will propose burst-resize; PayGlide SRE must authorize in the change advisory window.

We’ll include both an event timeline and the runbook snippet in the artifact bundle. Jonas will own the canary instrumentation; Monica will own the artifact retention steps.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: kv-warm-cold-scenarios.json

On Nov 7, 2028, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Dedicated pool is provisioned for Nov 7 02:00 PST — Nov 10 06:00 PST.

Run completed earlier today — quick preliminary notes while we digest the run artifacts:

- Phase A steady-state: peak observed 1,760 req/s sustained for 10m windows; p95 = 270ms, p99 = 640ms, overall error rate 0.28%. Looks within gate.
- Phase B cold-cache: cold-start-first-100 p95 = 2.1s, but we saw a small cluster of container restarts correlated with a kernel patch on one host — loadlab attached crash logs (run-2028-11-07-loadlab-report.pdf).
- Canary decision: manual hold. The canary did not trigger auto-rollback (criteria not exceeded), but PayGlide ops would prefer we remediate the host instability before pinning.

Requesting Redwood: please share the artifact bundle and a short remediation recommendation (hotfix vs host drain) and a proposed follow-up run window. Also confirm the artifact retention period and redaction tags for compliance.

Thanks all — excellent coordination.

Alicia
Head of Product, PayGlide
